parker-1981: Melissodes agilis, Pollination & Floral Ecology, Behavior, General Ecology, Melissodes agilis pollination efficiency, Melissodes agilis sunflower pollinator, Melissodes pollen load per visit, Melissodes vs honey bee seed set, Melissodes male patrolling and clustering behavior, Melissodes floral fidelity sunflower rows, Melissodes oligolecty on sunflower, Melissodes as most abundant wild bee. This field study at Logan, Utah compares pollination efficiency of native bees versus honey bees on sunflower, finding Melissodes agilis (both sexes) to be the most effective and most faithful pollinator across all sterile/fertile line combinations, producing far more seeds per visit than Apis mellifera and carrying substantially more pollen (up to ~104,500 grains per female) than any other bee group studied.
batra-1977: Melissodes floris, Life History & Nesting Biology, Natural Enemies & Biotic Interactions, Pollination & Floral Ecology, Behavior, Melissodes floris nest architecture, Melissodes floris burrow and cell structure, Melissodes floris nesting biology Guatemala, Phoridae parasitoid of Melissodes floris, Melissodes floris interspecific nest aggregation, Melissodes floris solitary nesting female, Melissodes floris provisioning behavior, Melissodes Eumelissodes subgenus nest description, Phoridae (phorid fly), parasitoid. This paper gives one of the few available nest descriptions for the genus Melissodes, documenting a complete nest of Melissodes floris (subgenus Eumelissodes) found within a dense multi-species bee aggregation on a roadside bank near San Miguel Duenas, Guatemala. It reports burrow and cell dimensions, provision character, and notes that three dead M. floris females each carried a puparium of a phorid fly (Phoridae) in the thorax, indicating parasitism of the bee by this fly.
cilla-2012: Melissodes tintinnans, Melissodes rufithorax, Pollination & Floral Ecology, General Ecology, Behavior, Methodology & Survey Techniques, Melissodes tintinnans sunflower pollen foraging, Melissodes rufithorax sunflower pollen foraging, Melissodes tintinnans eclectic oligolecty, Melissodes rufithorax broad oligolecty on Asteraceae, Melissodes scopal pollen load analysis, Melissodes field margin hedgerow foraging Argentina, Melissodes Ligustrum and Eucalyptus pollen use, Melissodes tintinnans and rufithorax phenology synchrony with Helianthus annuus bloom, Melissodes Pampean agroecosystem crop pollinator, Melissodes nesting aggregation crop pollination value. This paper reports the pollen foraging preferences of Melissodes (Ecplectica) tintinnans and M. (Ecplectica) rufithorax in a commercial sunflower field and its field margins near Carlos Casares, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, based on scopal and body-hair pollen load analysis over a full growing season. It shows both species rely heavily on Helianthus annuus pollen during bloom but shift to Bidens sp. and Baccharis sp. after bloom, classifying M. tintinnans as eclectic oligolectic and M. rufithorax as broadly oligolectic on Asteraceae, and highlights the role of hedgerow trees (Ligustrum, Eucalyptus) and field-margin vegetation in sustaining these populations as potential sunflower pollinators.
turner-1908: Behavior, Natural Enemies & Biotic Interactions, Melissodes sun-dance courtship display, Melissodes male mating swarm behavior, Melissodes nuptial pursuit and ambuscade, Melissodes female pollen return flight, Melissodes burrow nesting aggregation Augusta Georgia, Nomadidae (cuckoo bees) cleptoparasite of Melissodes, Melissodes clypeus color sexual dimorphism, Melissodes coition behavior, Nomadidae, cleptoparasite. This 1908 field note describes a male mating aggregation display ('sun-dance') observed at a Melissodes nesting site in Augusta, Georgia, in which yellow-clypeus males repeatedly chase, dodge, and grapple with black-clypeus females returning to their burrows carrying pollen loads, which Turner interprets as a 'nuptial ambuscade' facilitating copulation. It also notes Nomadidae (cuckoo bees), a cleptoparasitic bee family, loitering near Melissodes burrows waiting to oviposit on the bees' stored pollen provisions.

This is Part I of LaBerge's monographic revision of Melissodes for North and Central America, so far covering the introduction, phylogenetic and geographic-variation discussion, the key to subgenera, the complete subgenus Brachymelissodes (cressonii, minima), and a large part of subgenus Epimelissodes: full species accounts for M. atripes, M. albocollaris, M. grandissima, the newly described M. aegis, M. comanche, M. machaerantherae, M. helianthelli, the newly described M. nitida, an extensive account of M. obliqua with three subspecies (obliqua, expurgata, caliginosa) including a nesting-biology account (Custer, Colorado) describing Triepeolus concavus as a cleptoparasite, M. texana with the new subspecies M. texana eluta, M. petulca with its two subspecies (petulca, suffusa; with illinoensis and townsendi treated as synonyms), including a geographic pie-graph analysis of the Texas intergradation zone between the subspecies and extensive flower records dominated by Compositae (especially Helianthus (sunflower), Ratibida, Gaillardia, Rudbeckia, Coreopsis, and Helenium), and the start of the species account of M. sabinensis (Epimelissodes), a species of three largely allopatric subspecies distinguished from petulca suffusa mainly by male mesepisternal hair density and genitalic characters. THIS RECORD IS PARTIAL — only pages 911-1020 of a roughly 250-page work have been processed so far; topics/keywords/species/overview will be revised as later batches (covering the remaining subgenera and species) are added.
